answer: Trust spreads through the social graph like a short random walk: seeded honest nodes push credit along vouch edges, and each step can only ripple outward a few hops. A sybil cluster hangs off the real trellis by a handful of attack edges, so its whole cluster shares the trickle those edges carry. Every extra fake head dilutes that share, forcing the attacker to buy more real cross-links. Keys stay a cipher; only edge structure matters.
